name: Wu Xiaohui

summary.text: Wu Xiaohui is the founder and former chairman of China's Anbang Insurance Group. While he led Anbang, the company negotiated in early 2017 with Kushner Companies over the redevelopment of 666 Fifth Avenue; the talks ended by mutual agreement on 29 March 2017 after U.S. lawmakers raised conflict-of-interest concerns about Jared Kushner's White House role. On 10 May 2018 the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court sentenced Wu to 18 years in prison for fundraising fraud and embezzlement, deprived him of political rights for four years and confiscated 10.5 billion yuan of his property.

facts.claim: On 10 May 2018 the Shanghai Municipal No. 1 Intermediate People's Court sentenced Wu, former chairman of Anbang Insurance Group, to 18 years in prison for fundraising fraud and embezzlement.
facts.quote: The Shanghai Municipal No. 1 Intermediate People's Court announced the sentence Thursday.

facts.claim: The court also deprived Wu of his political rights for four years and confiscated 10.5 billion yuan (about $1.6 billion) of his property.
facts.quote: Wu was also deprived of his political rights for four years, and had 10.5 billion yuan (1.6 billion U.S. dollars) of his property confiscated

facts.claim: The court found that Wu had defrauded investors of more than 65.2 billion yuan by the time his violations came to light and had used his position to embezzle 10 billion yuan from Anbang.
facts.quote: The court also found that Wu had taken advantage of his position to illegally embezzle 10 billion yuan from Anbang.

facts.claim: Wu initially contested the charges at trial; in his closing statement he said he understood and regretted the crimes and asked for leniency.
facts.quote: In his closing statement he said he understood and regretted the crimes and requested leniency.

facts.claim: On 29 March 2017 Kushner Companies said it was no longer in discussions with Anbang about the potential redevelopment of 666 Fifth Avenue and that the firms had mutually agreed to end talks; five U.S. lawmakers had raised concerns with a White House ethics official about Anbang's ties to Jared Kushner through the deal.
facts.quote: Kushner Companies is no longer in discussions with Anbang about 666 Fifth Avenue's potential redevelopment, and our firms have mutually agreed to end talks regarding the property.

sources.title: Kushner, Anbang end Manhattan tower talks; other talks emerge
Kushner Companies and Anbang end talks on 666 Fifth Avenue

facts.claim: Reported terms of the abandoned deal varied: Bloomberg reported Anbang would pay $400 million to Kushner Companies as part of a $4 billion redevelopment, while the Wall Street Journal reported Anbang could provide up to $1.25 billion in equity; Anbang's spokesman told Caixin the insurer made no investment in the building.
facts.quote: Anbang's public relationship manager told Caixin that the insurer didn't make any investment in the office building.
